Jack — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, then a recommended MAP (mutual action plan):

High-level tradeoffs
- Marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP): fastest procurement for standard SKUs, supports card and invoice (depending on listing), easier for pilot/POC. Co-sell can apply if Redwood is in the appropriate partner program and AWS engages; that adds GTM benefits but may add 2–4 weeks to align partner registration and credits.
- Direct contract + SOW: best for enterprise terms (data residency, custom SLAs, longer-term discounts). Procurement lead time typically 3–8 weeks depending on internal PO cycles and legal negotiation.

Key differences to flag for Procurement
- Discounts: deeper, negotiable for direct commitments; marketplace often has published pricing but can be used with Marketplace Private Offers for negotiated pricing.
- Invoicing: marketplace sometimes supports marketplace billing; direct allows standard PO + invoice cadence.
- Support/SLA: we can attach SLA addenda to direct contracts; marketplace purchases map to standard support tiers (we can request premium support onboarding).

Attached: Redwood_AWS_CoSell_Checklist.pdf and Pricing_Comparison_worksheet.xlsx — quick reference. Also included a draft SOW for scope alignment (Acme_SOW_Draft_v3.docx).

Proposed MAP (summary)
1) Week 1: confirm pilot scope, choose procurement path (Marketplace pilot OR Direct PO pilot). Owner: Acme (Jack) + Redwood (Rafael).
2) Week 2: If Marketplace: enable private listing and send PO / card info. If Direct: Redwood sends SOW and T&Cs for review. Owner: Redwood (Monica) + Acme Procurement.
3) Week 3–5: Legal and billing alignment (timeline varies). If co-sell required, coordinate partner registration in parallel. Owner: Redwood Partnerships / Acme Procurement.
4) Week 5+: Pilot start, telemetry + cost monitoring.

If you want I can produce a one-page procurement brief for Finance that calls out exact gating items. Thoughts?

Jack — adding a bit more color from Solutions & Partnerships:

Marketplace specifics (AWS focus)- Co-sell eligibility: Redwood needs to be a registered AWS partner and list the product. If you want AWS co-sell to drive the sale, we request an internal AWS rep to accept the opportunity; that coordination can take 1–3 weeks after partner paperwork is in place.
- Private Offers: we can set up a Private Offer (negotiated price on the marketplace) which preserves marketplace billing while allowing your discounts and PO. That path is often the fastest way to get procurement to sign while still benefiting from marketplace workflows.

Direct contract specifics- Contract redlines: customers typically need 1–3 rounds of minor edits; major legal requests (e.g., indemnity additions, data residency clauses) can add time.
- Implementation SLA and onboarding credits: easier to bake into direct agreements.

Practical recommendation
- If timeline to start pilot is <30 days: Private Offer on AWS marketplace (we handle the offer + your procurement uses PO). This minimizes legal friction and supports card/invoice based on your procurement settings.
- If you need enterprise controls (custom SLAs, audit log retention policy in contract): go direct and we prioritize a fast-track legal review — we can often close within 4–6 weeks if scope is well-defined.

I can help draft the Private Offer paperwork and loop our partner manager at AWS (Maya) to expedite co-sell if you want that route.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
